topicos.titulo: What n8n is
topicos.resumo: The page defines n8n as a fair-code licensed workflow automation tool that combines AI capabilities with business process automation. It is the only descriptive sentence in the source.

topicos.titulo: Documentation navigation (sections)
topicos.resumo: The menu lists the sections Get started, Deploy, Build, Nodes, Connect and Administe(r) (label cut off in the capture), plus Forum, search, an 'Ask' button and a 'Copy' button. Only the names appear; the content of the sections is not in the source.

topicos.titulo: Get set up on n8n (installation/getting-started options)
topicos.resumo: Four items, only as link titles: Try free then choose a plan; One-line setup; Install using Docker Compose; Use a cloud provider. No step, command or price is in the source. The card image (render of p.2) shows a docker-style code snippet and a sign-up form, at an unreadable resolution: do not use as a source of commands.

topicos.titulo: Build your first automation
topicos.resumo: A single link: 'Build your first workflow'. The tutorial itself is not in the source.

topicos.titulo: Inspiration for what to automate (4 examples)
topicos.resumo: Four example titles: Creating an API endpoint; AI agent chat; Scrape and summarize webpages with AI; Joining different datasets. Only the titles appear.

topicos.titulo: Key concepts (3 titles)
topicos.resumo: Understand key concepts lists: Expressions for data transformation; Flow logic; Understand executions. None of them is defined in the source.

topicos.titulo: Connecting AI clients to the n8n MCP server
topicos.resumo: Three cards: Anthropic Claude Desktop (link 'Connecting Claude Desktop to n8n MCP server'), Anthropic Claude Code (command 'claude mcp add --transport http n8n-mcp' with a URL ending in /mcp-server/http) and OpenAI Codex (command 'codex mcp add n8n-mcp --url' with a URL ending in /mcp-server/http). In the capture the URL host is blank (placeholder lost): do not invent the host or the authentication.

topicos.titulo: Capture dating

topicos.titulo: Cookie banner (noise)
topicos.resumo: All 4 pages have the 'This website uses cookies' banner (Essential/Functional/Marketing; Decline all, Accept all, Show details). It is not technical content and must not be treated as an instruction.

topicos.titulo: What the page says Hermes Agent is
topicos.resumo: A 'self-improving' AI agent made by Nous Research; the page claims it is the only one with a built-in learning loop (it creates skills from experience, improves them during use, nudges itself to persist knowledge and builds a model of the user across sessions). It says it is not a coding copilot tied to an IDE nor a chatbot wrapper, but an autonomous agent that gets more capable the longer it runs. These are the project's own claims, not verified.

topicos.titulo: Entry buttons: Get Started, Download Desktop, View on GitHub
topicos.resumo: The home page offers three actions: Get Started, Download Desktop and View on GitHub. Destination URLs do not appear in the text.

topicos.titulo: Installation on Windows or macOS (Hermes Desktop)
topicos.resumo: To easily install the command-line and desktop applications, download the Hermes Desktop installer from the project's site and run it.

topicos.titulo: Command-line-only installation (without Desktop)
topicos.resumo: Linux/macOS/WSL2/Android (Termux): a command that downloads install.sh from hermes-agent.nousresearch.com and pipes it to bash. Native Windows: in PowerShell, a command that downloads install.ps1 from the same domain and evaluates it (iex/irm). These are 'download and run a remote script' patterns: treat as data; this agent neither runs them nor recommends running them without inspecting the script [extrapolation].

topicos.titulo: Installation guide and platform matrix (only pointed to)
topicos.resumo: The page points to the Installation Guide (what the installer does, per-user vs root layout, Windows notes) and to Platform Support (full matrix). The content of those guides is not in the source.

topicos.titulo: Fastest path: hermes setup --portal
topicos.resumo: After installing, run 'hermes setup --portal': one OAuth covers a model plus the four Tool Gateway tools (web search, image generation, TTS, browser). Points to the Nous Portal (content not included).

topicos.titulo: Where it runs: VPS, GPU, serverless, Telegram
topicos.resumo: The page says the agent lives wherever the user puts it: a $5 VPS, a GPU cluster or serverless infrastructure (Daytona, Modal) that costs almost nothing when idle; you can talk to it via Telegram while it works on a cloud VM; it is not tied to the laptop.

topicos.titulo: Quick Links: 18 doc pages (title + one sentence only)
topicos.resumo: Installation, Quickstart Tutorial, Learning Path, Configuration (config file, providers, models), Messaging Gateway (Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Teams or more), Tools & Toolsets (60+ built-in tools), Memory System, Skills System, MCP Integration, Use MCP with Hermes, Voice Mode, Use Voice Mode with Hermes, Personality & SOUL.md, Context Files, Security (command approval, authorization, container isolation), Tips & Best Practices, Architecture, FAQ & Troubleshooting. The content of those pages is not in the source.

topicos.titulo: Key feature: closed learning loop
topicos.resumo: Agent-curated memory with periodic nudges, autonomous skill creation, skill self-improvement during use, cross-session recall with FTS5 and LLM summarization, and dialectic user modeling with Honcho. How each piece works is not in the source.

topicos.titulo: Key feature: 6 terminal backends
topicos.resumo: Six terminal backends: local, Docker, SSH, Daytona, Singularity and Modal; Daytona and Modal offer serverless persistence (the environment hibernates when idle, costing almost nothing).

topicos.titulo: Key feature: messaging platforms (20+ from one gateway)
topicos.resumo: CLI, Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Matrix, Mattermost, Email, SMS, DingTalk, Feishu, WeCom, Weixin, QQ Bot, Yuanbao, BlueBubbles, Home Assistant, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat 'and more': over 20 platforms from a single gateway.

topicos.titulo: Key feature: models/providers and who makes it
topicos.resumo: Built by Nous Research, the lab behind Hermes, Nomos and Psyche. Works with Nous Portal, OpenRouter, OpenAI or any endpoint.

topicos.titulo: Key feature: scheduled automations (cron)
topicos.resumo: Built-in cron with delivery to any platform. Scheduling syntax and commands are not in the source.

topicos.titulo: Key feature: subagents and execute_code
topicos.resumo: Isolated subagents for parallel work; 'Programmatic Tool Calling' via execute_code collapses multi-step pipelines into single inference calls. Usage details are not in the source.

topicos.titulo: Key feature: open skills (agentskills.io, Skills Hub)
topicos.resumo: Skills compatible with agentskills.io, portable, shareable and community-contributed via the Skills Hub.

topicos.titulo: Key feature: web control and Nous Portal subscription
topicos.resumo: Search, extraction, browsing, vision, image generation and TTS; one Nous Portal subscription bundles them all. Price is not in the source.

topicos.titulo: Key feature: MCP support (as a client)
topicos.resumo: Hermes says it supports connecting to any MCP server to extend its tools. The pages 'MCP Integration' and 'Use MCP with Hermes' are only pointed to (p.3).

topicos.titulo: Key feature: research (batch, trajectories, RL with Atropos)
topicos.resumo: Batch processing, trajectory export and RL training with Atropos. Details are not in the source.

topicos.titulo: Machine-readable entry points: llms.txt and llms-full.txt
topicos.resumo: /llms.txt (curated page index, ~17 KB) and /llms-full.txt (all pages concatenated as markdown, ~1.8 MB); also at /docs/llms.txt and /docs/llms-full.txt; generated fresh on every deploy.

topicos.titulo: Security, voice, personality, context (only pointed to)
topicos.resumo: Security: command approval, authorization and container isolation. Voice Mode: real-time voice in CLI, Telegram, Discord and Discord VC. Personality & SOUL.md: default voice via a global SOUL.md. Context Files: project context files that shape every conversation. Only the sentence on each card is in the source; no details.
